patch_description: Key insight: a centrally symmetric point set (points ±v_k) has diameter exactly 2R. So pick 7 well-separated unit directions (the Tammes/spherical-code problem for N=7, optimal min chord distance ≈ 1.2567, i.e. angle ≈ 77.87°) and output each direction with its antipode → 14 points with dmax=2 and dmin = min chord distance, giving ratio ≈ 0.63 (squared ≈ 0.39), well above the reference 0.24. The program solves the 7-point Tammes problem via annealed soft-min tangent-space gradient ascent on the unit sphere from many diverse starts (pentagonal bipyramid, Fibonacci lattice, jittered bipyramids, random), then an exact SLSQP polish (maximize t s.t. chord distances ≥ t, all points on the sphere). Finally it stacks ±directions, verifies the true 14-point ratio with the true metric, and normalizes diameter to 1. This is a fundamentally different reduction of the problem compared to generic free-space min/max optimization.
